hero.title: Switzerland: Masters in Automobile Engineering for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: A Master’s in Automobile Engineering in Switzerland is a good choice for students who are interested in automotive design, electric vehicles, vehicle dynamics, autonomous driving, powertrain technology and sustainable mobility. In Switzerland you can learn the state-of-the-art engineering and conduct research in areas like mechanical engineering, robotics, control systems and energy-efficient transportation.

overview: The master’s in Mechanical Engineering at ETH Zurich usually lasts 1.5 years (90 ECTS credits). EPFL’s Mechanical Engineering master’s is based on 120 ECTS credits and generally takes two years to complete. Double degree paths can have their own study plans.
### 3\. Can Indian students study automotive-related subjects in English?

Yes, the Master in Mechanical Engineering at ETH Zurich is taught in English. EPFL offers courses in English and French and students should check the language requirements for their chosen modules and degree route.

items: ### 3\. Can Indian students study automotive-related subjects in English?

Yes, the Master in Mechanical Engineering at ETH Zurich is taught in English. EPFL offers courses in English and French and students should check the language requirements for their chosen modules and degree route.
### 4\. How much will it cost overall?

Using the estimates in this guide, budget around ₹31.81–52.27 lakh for a 1.5-year program and ₹42.42–69.70 lakh for a two-year program. Actual costs will vary depending on the university and your lifestyle
#### 5\. Can I work in Switzerland after I graduate?

Potentially, but employment is not guaranteed. You will need to find appropriate employment and satisfy the relevant Swiss immigration and work-permit requirements. Automotive related opportunities also depend on the employer, technical specialization and experience.
